resolutions.researcher_notes: Status 'operating' is inferred, not literal (per confidence_tiers guidance). No independent source names 'Abu Ali-Berri gas pipeline' specifically; the specific line traces only to the dead steel-network.com Arabic article (cite 3 on gem.wiki, not in Wayback) and OPEC ASB aggregates. Both endpoints are documented operating facilities: Saudipedia says Berri Gas Plant has operated since 1977 as part of Aramco's main gas network; nsenergybusiness confirms the existing Abu Ali GOSP facility and that Saudi Aramco owns and operates the Berri field (in production 4+ decades). Operating status of the connecting gas line is a reasonable contextual inference, not a directly-sourced fact.

Fuel=Gas well supported: Saudipedia describes Berri Gas Plant as a facility within Saudi Aramco's main gas network that processes gas and supplies natural gas to the Master Gas System. The Abu Ali-Berri line is a gas pipeline feeding the Berri Gas Plant, so Gas is consistent. One strong source (medium).

StartYear1=2008 could not be independently verified. The only source for 2008 is the dead steel-network.com Arabic article (gem.wiki cite 3), which is not archived in Wayback and returns no snapshot. The nearby Khursaniyah gas program / Abu Ali GOSP came online ~Dec 2007-2008, which makes a 2008 start plausible, but no source ties a 2008 in-service date to this specific Abu Ali-Berri gas line. OPEC ASB 2011/2012 (gem cites 1,2) are national aggregate statistics that do not document individual pipeline start years. Not fabricating a ref; UNRESOLVED.

LengthKnown=44 km could not be independently verified. The 44 km (and 30-inch diameter) figures trace solely to the dead steel-network.com Arabic article (gem.wiki cite 3), unarchived in Wayback. No independent trade/technical source (Aramco, MEED, OGJ, nsenergybusiness, Saipem) states a length for this line. UNRESOLVED.

FuelSource=Abu Ali Island partially supported: nsenergybusiness documents the existing Abu Ali GOSP facility (a Saudi Aramco gas-oil separation plant on Abu Ali Island near Jubail) that separates associated gas, consistent with Abu Ali Island being the upstream/source end of a gas line to Berri. The source confirms Abu Ali Island is a real Aramco hydrocarbon-processing point but does not explicitly name it as this pipeline's fuel source. Low tier.

Location values well corroborated by two independent sources. Saudipedia places the Berri Gas Plant in al-Jubayl (Al Jubail) Industrial City, Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia. nsenergybusiness places the Berri field production/processing facilities and the Abu Ali GOSP in Jubail, Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia. Both endpoints (Abu Ali Island start, Berri Gas Plant end at Al Jubail) sit in the Eastern Province. Supports EndLocation=Berri Gas Plant, EndPrefecture=Al Jubail, Start/End State=Eastern Province, Country=Saudi Arabia.

Owner1=Saudi Aramco (100%) well corroborated by two independent sources. nsenergybusiness: 'State-owned Saudi Aramco owns and operates the Berri field.' Saudipedia: the Berri Gas Plant is a facility within Saudi Aramco's main gas network. Both Berri-field/plant assets and the Abu Ali GOSP are Saudi Aramco assets; sole 100% Aramco ownership is consistent with all Saudi upstream/midstream hydrocarbon infrastructure.
